Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking our SIG last week. The reviewers on our side have a few follow-ups specific to audit records and chain-of-custody for CAIQ items:

- Can you confirm the canonical set of admin-action fields you persist for the platform (examples: actor_id, action, target, pre_state_hash, request_id, trace_id, ip, user_agent, kv_cache_eviction)?
- What is the default retention for privileged admin events, and what options exist for 3+ year retention?
- For export, do you support a signed manifest + per-file checksum (HMAC or SHA256) and delivery via S3 (encrypted) and also a streaming endpoint for live pulls?
- How do you handle timezone normalization and timestamp fidelity across regions? Any recommended normalization for legal review?
- We may need an attested chain-of-custody (signed manifest, timestamping, delivery evidence) suitable for our compliance team—what's the turnaround to produce a sample bundle?

I attached the SIG questionnaire excerpt that asks about evidence artifacts (SIG_questionnaire.pdf). If you can point us at the specific export schema and a sample manifest, that would help our legal & infra folks review.

Thanks,

Expect a short technical packet from Ben within 24 hours and a timeline from me in the next business day.

Best,

Gabriel — hi, quick technical breakdown of what we persist and how we deliver: (TL;DR: default retention 365d, extendable; exports can be signed + encrypted; streaming with checkpointing)

Canonical admin event schema (examples of persisted fields):
- event_ts_utc (ISO8601)
- event_seq (monotonic sequence id)
- actor_id (internal user id or service principal)
- actor_email (when available)
- actor_role
- action (create/update/delete/assume_role/privileged_op)
- target_resource (bucket/instance/model_id/route)
- operation_start_ms, operation_end_ms
- request_id (UUID)
- trace_id (opentelemetry link)
- prev_state_hash (SHA256 of canonical JSON of prior state when applicable)
- delta_blob (short base64 diff when allowed)
- kv_cache_eviction (bool)
- actor_ip, user_agent
- service_version, region

Retention and extension: default retention is 365 days for admin events. For enterprise contracts we support extended retention tiers (2 years, 5 years) and can provision immutable archival buckets with object lock for legal holds. Note: extended retention requires a short MSA addendum.

Export formats and proof-of-custody:
- Snapshot bundles: gzipped newline-delimited JSON files + a signed manifest.csv that lists filenames, record counts, SHA256 checksums, and HMACs. Manifest is signed with our platform signing key; we can also notarize via timestamping service on request.
- Streaming: secure, token-authenticated streaming (TLS + mutual TLS option) that emits checkpoint tokens every N records. The checkpoint token contains the stream offset and an HMAC so the receiver can prove contiguous ingestion.
- Delivery options: S3 (server-side encrypted SSE-KMS) bucket + presigned URL or direct put to a customer-managed bucket. We support SFTP handoffs for legal teams that require it.

Timezone handling: all timestamps exported normalized to UTC. We include original local_ts_local and tz_offset fields where available. We also include event_seq to guarantee total ordering for playback.

Attachments: export_schema_v2.json (schema) and a sample_manifest.csv (attached) showing the manifest format.

Let me know if you need the manifest signed by a third-party timestamp service; we can add that to the runbook.

-ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Gabriel — a couple legal notes to help you evaluate the bundle:
- When we provide snapshots containing user identifiers or other PII, we include a redacted and full version controlled delivery option. Redaction rules are configurable but default to obfuscating email/local part + replacing IPs with CIDR block if requested.
- Chain-of-custody: our attested manifest includes: manifest signature, HMACs per file, server-side delivery logs (S3 put receipts), and a signed delivery receipt from our compliance team. We can provide an attestation letter and chained log entries suitable for SIG/CAIQ review.
- Timeline: operationally we can produce a signed sample snapshot + manifest within 3 business days. For a full attested package (HSM-signed + timestamp service), allow 7 business days due to cross-team coordination.

If Novaline needs a contractual SLA for export turnaround, we'll need to capture that in an addendum.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
